handbookNote: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System', cover-dated September 9, 2022, base content Version: July 2017), published by the Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV) -- fetched directly from https://www.in.gov/bmv/files/cdl-manual.pdf on 2026-08-22 (5.2MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext to scratchpad/in_cdl_research/cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,367 lines), supplemented by the official 'Indiana Specific Commercial Driver's License Applicant Information' document (form SP 283, R-5 7/26), fetched from https://www.in.gov/bmv/licenses-permits-ids/files/indiana-specific-cdl-manual.pdf on 2026-08-22 (6 pages of real content extracted via pdftotext to scratchpad/in_cdl_research/in_cdl_manual_plain.txt) -- price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: unlike several other CDL-track states already built in this project (e.g. Idaho, which has its own official per-test item-count table), NEITHER official Indiana source -- not the base AAMVA manual, not the Indiana-specific BMV supplement -- states an exact knowledge-test question count or number-correct-to-pass for any Indiana CDL test (general knowledge or any endorsement). Several third-party test-prep sites claim '50 questions, 40 correct to pass' for Indiana's general knowledge test, but this figure could not be confirmed on any official IN.gov source and is therefore NOT asserted as fact anywhere in this question bank -- per this project's no-default-values discipline, this is explicitly hedged rather than borrowed from another state or an unverified third party. What IS confirmed directly from the Indiana-specific BMV supplement: the federally standardized 80% minimum passing score applies (49 CFR 383.135(a), same as all other CDL-track states in this project); Indiana's six CDL endorsement codes are T (Double/Triple Trailers), P (Passenger Transport), N (Tank Vehicle), H (Hazardous Material), X (Combination Tank+Hazmat), and S (School Bus) -- notably Indiana does NOT use a 'C' Charter Bus endorsement (unlike Illinois) or an 'O' endorsement; Indiana's CDL restriction-code table (E, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, V, X, Z) is unusually granular, including a since-discontinued 'Q -- Bus Only' restriction; a CLP is valid for one year and must be held at least 14 days before the CDL skills test may be attempted; an out-of-state CDL must be transferred to Indiana within 30 days; CLP/CDL age minimums are 18 (21 to operate in interstate commerce or add a school bus endorsement); and a CDL expired/revoked/disqualified more than 3 years requires full retesting as a first-time applicant. Content-depth rationale: Indiana uses the AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual (the newer AAMVA revision, same generation as Idaho's 2022 CDL Testing System manual) organized into 13 sections -- Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes A/B/C, endorsements, CMV definitions, medical certification, disqualifications, testing structure), Section 2 Driving Safely (by far the largest section: vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing, communicating, speed/space management, hazard perception, distracted/aggressive driving, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, mountain driving, emergency maneuvers, skid control, ABS, accidents, fires, alcohol/drugs, fatigue, and hazmat rules for all drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (communication rules/shipping papers/placarding plus loading/driving/emergency rules -- the second-largest section), Section 10 School Bus, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving -- plus Indiana-specific administrative detail layered in from the BMV supplement for the licensing bucket. Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in Indiana's manual, and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger states. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Indiana manual text or the Indiana-specific BMV supplement cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
